svg.title: MILES at test time: confidence routing, memory WRITE on confident samples, memory READ on uncertain samples
svg.desc: A frozen LLM answers each incoming test question K = 10 times; answer agreement against a threshold tau routes it. Confident questions take the WRITE path: the majority vote becomes a pseudo-label and the answer, and MCTS over reasoning states (Layer-1 similarity sampling, reward r = 1 if the rollout matches the pseudo-label) yields (state, unit, correctness) tuples for per-unit datasets plus (step-goal, step) seeds; k-means clusters of seeds are summarized by the LLM into new memory units, and each unit's binary selection head is trained with BCE. Each memory unit holds a sub-goal key g_i (1536-d embedding), a sub-instruction u_i, an effective threshold, a context codebook, and a head. Uncertain questions take the READ path: memory-guided tree search retrieves 16 candidates by cosine similarity to the keys (Layer 1), reranks them with the learned heads over codebook max-similarity features (Layer 2), applies the top sub-instruction to write the next step, and majority-votes over the response pool. The bottom strip shows the selection objective, its KL-regularized closed-form optimum, and the per-unit one-vs-rest BCE surrogate used to train the heads.
